transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i know you had a packed day, we wanted to run through quicklaunch fit and hosting options and make sure the quickstart gets you to first token fast
[00:12] Lena (Hydra): thanks maya, yep excited, we basically need a path to validate model quality and cost within 2 weeks, and we want to understand whether hosted makes sense or we need dedicated or private right away
[00:24] Maya: totally, that's what we'll cover — i'll go through the PLG/self-serve route first (free credits, ttft, quickstart) and then raj will field deeper infra questions around dedicated/private and perf
[00:37] Raj (Redwood SE): hi all, quick hi, i'll try to keep it high level first then dig in — i'm raj. just to set context, are you planning PROD in 3 months or is this an experiment?
[00:49] Marcus (CTO): more of an experiment with a clear prod gating criteria — if latency < 200ms p50 for our chat feature and cost < $0.002 per 1k tokens then we consider next steps
[01:05] Priya (Dev Lead): also we have strict data retention and residency needs — logs need to remain in our VPC for a pilot, and we need SSO + SAML for user access
[01:16] Maya: perfect, so for quickstart we normally provide a hosted PLG API account with credits — that gives you immediate TTFT: usually under an hour to make first request if you follow the quickstart doc. we'll include SDK snippets for node/python and a sample postman collection
[01:32] Lena: when you say credits, what's typical? we want enough to run a small benchmark and a handful of dev tests
[01:38] Maya: we can provision 100k tokens to start, expandable if you need it. that's usually enough for functional tests and a 30-minute realistic throughput benchmark
[01:48] Marcus: ok, and for latency — hosted shared tenancy, can you hit our 200ms p50? what's realistic for gen tasks?
[02:00] Raj: so depends on model family and sequence length. hosted uses our multi-tenant pools; for medium seq lengths (<=512) and efficient llama-family variants we commonly see p50s ~80-150ms for small/medium models. multi-tenant introduces some variance at p95. if you need tight SLOs we recommend dedicated capacity which gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency
[02:22] Priya: got it. Is there a middle ground? like burst capacity or reserved but less than full dedicated commitment?
[02:30] Raj: yes, we have burst and reserved configs — you can reserve a baseline and allow bursts to shared capacity. that often hits the sweet spot for teams that need predictability for peak traffic but don't want 24/7 reserved spend
[02:44] Lena: what's the private option look like? full VPC or on-prem?
[02:50] Raj: private = VPC deployment where the control plane is customer-managed or a private control plane with network peering, plus an optional on-prem package that we ship for air-gapped environments. integrates with your KMS/HSM for key management and supports audit log forwarding
[03:05] Marcus: if we do private VPC for pilot, can you still give us the quickstart credits? we don't want a slow handshake to try things
[03:13] Maya: we can do a hybrid: provision hosted credits for dev teams to iterate immediately while we stand up a VPC pilot in parallel. teams often do that to get TTFT low while the infra work completes
[03:26] Priya: that feels workable — what's the typical lead time to get a VPC pilot?
[03:31] Raj: typically 2-4 weeks depending on approvals and IP whitelisting. on-prem is longer because of shipping and site install. for VPC, we need network details, outbound egress rules, and an IAM contact for SSO integration
[03:46] Marcus: we need SOC2, ISO docs, and a data processing addendum — do you have a compliance pack?
[03:52] Maya: yes, we'll share the SOC2 report, ISO attestation, and a standard DPA. i'll attach them after the call. also include a short security FAQ that answers KMS, log retention, and RBAC
[04:07] Lena: excellent. a couple infra specifics for the SE — raj, can you explain caching and the KV cache thing? our docs mention KV cache but our SREs confuse it with something else
[04:16] Raj: sure — we do prefix/KV caching at the serving runtime level. it stores attention key/value states to avoid recomputing long context for repeated prefixes. i've seen folks call it the KV "cash" in notes, so that might be the source of confusion — it's pronounced K-V cache. it helps lower token cost and improves latency for repeated contexts
[04:36] Priya: and does that work across sessions or just per-instance?
[04:40] Raj: it's per model variant and shard — we can persist caches for a shard to warm subsequent requests. for multi-tenant hosted it's ephemeral, but for dedicated/private we can configure more aggressive warming and sharing strategies
[04:52] Marcus: what about model variants and quantization? we plan to use a quantized model to reduce cost but worried about quality loss
[04:59] Raj: we recommend starting with a quantized variant we validated — we provide model recommendations and quantization profiles by workload. you can A/B via rollout policies in the console to catch regressions. Redwood Optimize will also suggest quantization levels for minimal quality drop
[05:18] Maya: do you want me to show the quickstart flow now? it's a 5-step checklist: sign up, create API key, SDK install, sample request, check logs
[05:25] Lena: yes please, a quick walkthrough would help the team feel comfortable
[05:28] Maya: ok — signing up is self-serve; we'll provision the credits on our backend. API keys are created per project, you can rotate keys and bind them to routes and RBAC. SDK has a one-liner. sample request — i'll paste a small payload in the chat after the call
[05:46] Priya: any rate limits? our devs want to run concurrent tests
[05:50] Maya: default trial rate limits are conservative; we can temporarily raise them for your benchmark window — raj will coordinate the exact numbers in the benchmark script
[05:59] Raj: i'll propose a script that ramps to your target concurrency and measures p50/p95; we can run it from our infra or you can run it from inside your VPC if you prefer
[06:09] Marcus: we'd prefer run from our env to replicate network egress and latency
[06:13] Raj: makes sense, we'll provide the script and a small docker image that runs the load and reports token counts. note that for TTL caching and warm-up the first 2-3 minutes tend to be worse, so we'll run a warm-up stage
[06:27] Lena: ok good — security question: does hosted store logs with PII? we need to make sure nothing persists outside our control for trial runs
[06:36] Maya: hosted by default stores minimal logs for debugging and metrics. we can enable data retention policies and redaction. for anything sensitive we recommend private/VPC where logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and reside in your account
[06:53] Priya: and what about key management for embeddings/eval data?
[07:00] Raj: for private we integrate with your cloud KMS or HSM; hosted supports envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for some tiers — but full HSM-backed key control is available in private/on-prem installs
[07:13] Marcus: do you have an SLA for dedicated? our product needs 99.9 availability during market hours
[07:20] Raj: yes dedicated comes with SLA tiers — we can map the SLA to the reserved capacity contract. hosted has best-effort Uptime, but enterprise customers on dedicated get contractual uptime and latency guarantees
[07:33] Lena: curious about cost math — what's the unit cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
[07:38] Maya: hosted is usage-based per-token, typical for PLG. dedicated is a committed monthly cost plus smaller usage add-ons; for high volume it's usually cheaper per-token but requires commit. we can run a TCO calc once we have projected QPS and sequence lengths
[07:55] Marcus: timeline wise, if we do quickstart now, and we want to go dedicated for prod in 3 months, when do we need to start the dedicated procurement?
[08:04] Maya: i'd start procurement conversations in 4-6 weeks so hardware reservations and capacity planning align; technically we can onboard to dedicated in 2-6 weeks depending on region and model choices
[08:17] Priya: any gotchas with SSO? we use Okta, want SCIM provisioning and SAML2 SSO
[08:23] Raj: we support Okta SAML and SCIM for provisioning. for private setups we can sync groups into RBAC and map to routes — we'll need your IdP admin contact and metadata file
[08:35] Lena: wonderful. one more developer workflow question: how long to get a working embedding index up and running for semantic search?
[08:44] Raj: embeddings are quick — index build time depends on dataset size. for 10k docs you can have an index and initial retrieval in under an hour on hosted; for larger datasets we advise batching and using our ingestion pipelines. we support vector stores connectors as well
[09:00] Marcus: ok that's helpful. can we talk about data residency — we have EU customers and need EU-only processing
[09:07] Maya: yes — we have region selection for hosted and can pin workloads to EU-only regions. for full control, private VPC in the EU region is recommended. we'll include region docs in the pack
[09:20] Priya: any chance you have sample benchmarks for LLama2-like models vs gpt-style? we've seen inconsistent numbers across vendors
[09:29] Raj: we publish verified perf profiles for model families — i'll link the internal perf digest. caveat: numbers vary with sequence length, quantization, and kernel selection. part of the benchmark we propose will run the exact model variant you plan to use to avoid surprises
[09:48] Maya: ok quick segue — onboarding checklist and responsibilities: redwood will provide credits, security pack, and benchmark script. hydra will provide dataset samples, ip allowlist, and idp metadata. is that accurate?
[10:01] Lena: yes, and hydra will also assign an SRE to work with raj for the benchmark run (priya will coordinate)
[10:09] Priya: yep i'll be the SRE contact and will share the ingress/egress rules and sample data by friday
[10:15] Marcus: what's the expected fallout if we hit model regressions during rollout? do you support rollbacks?
[10:20] Raj: yes — console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies to previous model variants. we also have eval hooks to compare quality metrics against a golden set; if a regression threshold is crossed it can auto-fallback and create an alert
[10:36] Lena: any limitations on function-calling / tool calling in hosted trial? we want to test tool calling to our internal lookup table
[10:44] Maya: function/tool calling is supported in hosted; you can wire a function schema in the sample app. for private you'd have even tighter network integration for calling internal services
[10:54] Priya: great. who will run the next call? we'd like a live benchmark and a short demo of quickstart flow
[10:58] Maya: i'll run a quickstart demo and raj will run the benchmark. let's tentatively schedule the benchmark session on 2028-09-21 at 15:00 UTC — does that work?
[11:08] Marcus: yes that's fine
[11:11] Lena: works for me
[11:13] Priya: good
[11:15] Maya: perfect. i'm going to recap: 1) redwood provisions PLG trial with 100k tokens, 2) redwood sends SOC2/compliance pack and pricing, 3) raj shares benchmark script, 4) hydra shares dataset, allowlist, and idp metadata. next call is benchmark on 09/21. any objections?
[11:33] Marcus: none here, sounds good
[11:35] Lena: no objections
[11:36] Priya: all good
[11:38] Maya: awesome — last housekeeping, you'll get a calendar invite for the benchmark with a link to the docker image and the script in the body. i'll also add a note about expected warm-up behavior and suggested concurrency curves
[11:51] Raj: one small technical aside — if you plan to use embeddings heavily, consider using our caching layer plus an embedding batch size that matches the GPU memory target; i'll include suggested params in the script
[12:03] Priya: thanks, that will help. any questions left on compliance?
[12:08] Marcus: none right now, i'll review the docs once they're in our tracker
[12:11] Lena: ok thanks everyone.
[12:13] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with materials and a trial account. talk soon.
[12:18] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings present (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "VP-C" for VPC or "sammel" for SAML), some speaker overlaps, filler words and truncated sentences typical of a remote sales sync.
